evidence: Cic. Off. 1.90: īdem semper vultus eademque frōns
terms.comment: “The same as” is īdem quī … or īdem atque (ac) …: idem velle atque idem nōlle, wanting and not wanting the same things (Sall. C. 20, Lewis & Short). Masculine īdem with a long i, neuter idem with a short one.

evidence: Ter. And. 3.2.31: multa concurrunt simul (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 2.12.1: ūnō tempore mihi datās duās
terms.comment: Also ūnō tempore, at one and the same time.

phrases.latin: ūna domus erat, īdem vīctus, isque commūnis
phrases.english: there was one house, the same food, and that shared

phrases.latin: praeclāraque est aequābilitās in omnī vītā et īdem semper vultus eademque frōns
phrases.english: and a fine thing is evenness all through life, always the same face and the same brow

phrases.latin: quid est sapientia? semper idem velle atque idem nōlle
phrases.english: what is wisdom? Always to want the same thing and refuse the same thing

phrases.latin: haec quae Pīcēnīs venit subducta trapētīs inchoat atque eadem fīnit olīva dapēs
phrases.english: the olive that comes fresh from the presses of Picenum begins the meal, and the same olive ends it
